--- title: "[MultiResponseGAM]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Multi-response GAM. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/feat-ppc/whittaker/multi_response.py#L93-L474){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python MultiResponseGAM( responses, formula, *, response_formulas=None, family=None, correlation="independent" ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Fits multiple response variables jointly against a common set of covariates, optionally sharing smooth terms (same basis and formula structure, though each response still gets its own coefficients) and estimating the residual correlation between responses. Internally, each response is fit as its own `GAM` using the shared formula plus any response-specific additional terms; what makes this a genuinely multivariate model rather than just several independent fits is the optional joint residual covariance structure, which is useful for understanding how responses co-vary after accounting for the shared covariates, and for joint (GLS-style) prediction via `joint_predict()`. Use `MultiResponseGAM` when you have several related outcomes measured on the same units (e.g. multiple biomarkers, or several pollutant concentrations) that likely share similar covariate relationships and whose residuals may be correlated. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [responses]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of response variable names (at least two). [formula]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Shared formula applied to all responses (e.g. `"s(x1) + s(x2)"`). The response side (before `~`, if present) is ignored; use `responses` to specify the response variables. [response_formulas]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[str, str] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Dict mapping response name to a response-specific formula string (covariates only, e.g., `{"y1": "s(x3)"}`) added on top of the shared formula for that response only. [family]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Family | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Response distribution family (applied to all responses). Defaults to `Gaussian()`. [correlation]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["independent"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Residual correlation structure: `"independent"` (default), which fits each response's `GAM` independently with no cross-response covariance modeling, or `"unstructured"`, which additionally estimates a full `k x k` residual covariance matrix from the fitted residuals. ::: ## Notes {.doc-notes} Under `correlation="unstructured"`, after each response's GAM is fit, the residual matrix `R \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times k}` (columns are `y_j - \hat y_j` for each response `j`) is used to estimate the residual covariance, $$\hat\Sigma = \frac{R^\top R}{n - 1},$$ and the corresponding correlation matrix by rescaling to unit diagonal. This does not feed back into how the individual response GAMs are fit (each is still fit marginally), but it is used by `joint_predict()` to report a joint covariance alongside the stacked mean predictions, and by `residual_correlation()` for diagnosing cross-response dependence. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#74e7b74a .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np from whittaker.multi_response import MultiResponseGAM rng = np.random.default_rng(0) n = 400 x = rng.uniform(0, 1, n) shared = np.sin(2 * np.pi * x) y1 = shared + rng.normal(scale=0.2, size=n) y2 = 0.5 * shared + rng.normal(scale=0.2, size=n) model = MultiResponseGAM(["y1", "y2"], "s(x)", correlation="unstructured") model.fit({"x": x, "y1": y1, "y2": y2}) print(model.residual_correlation()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` ResidualCorrelation: y1 y2 y1 1.000 -0.019 y2 -0.019 1.000 ``` ::: ::: ## Attributes {.doc-attributes}
Name Description
correlation Residual correlation structure used when fitting.
is_fitted Whether `fit()` has been called successfully.
n_responses Number of response variables modeled jointly.
responses List of response variable names, in the order passed to the constructor.
### [correlation]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Residual correlation structure used when fitting. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [correlation]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ### [is_fitted]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Whether `fit()` has been called successfully. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [is_fitted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ### [n_responses]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Number of response variables modeled jointly. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [n_responses]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ### [responses]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} List of response variable names, in the order passed to the constructor. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [responses]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods}
Name Description
